talk: Good forecasts aren't guesses, they're sums. Take what's already done, add what's already booked, then add the days left times your daily run rate. Multiply by the average value and you're done.

terms.meaning: Already delivered and counted. Completed orders, tickets scanned.
Promised but not delivered yet. Orders placed, seats reserved.
What you do on an average day or week. The engine of every forecast.

questions.prompt: The season ticket deadline is in 10 days. 4,200 are paid, 600 are reserved and waiting on payment. You're selling 80 a day. How many will you close at?
questions.hint: Done + booked + (days left x per day).
working: Forgetting the 600 already booked is the classic miss.
whyNot: 4,200 + 600 = 4,800 counts what's paid and booked but forgets the 10 days of selling still to come.
4,200 + 800 = 5,000 adds the future sales but drops the 600 reserved seats. They're booked, so count them.
That counts the future sales twice: 5,600 + 800 = 6,400. Each day's sales only go in once.

questions.prompt: Club shop, 4 days left in the month. 300 orders are delivered and 90 are packed and shipping. You get 30 orders a day and they ship the next day. How many orders count this month?
questions.hint: Orders placed on the last day ship next month.
working: Orders placed on the last day ship next month, so only 3 of the 4 days count.
whyNot: 300 + 90 = 390 stops at today. Orders keep coming for 3 more days that still ship this month.
300 + 4 x 30 = 420 counts all 4 days but forgets the 90 orders already packed and shipping.
300 + 90 + 4 x 30 = 510 counts all 4 days. Orders placed on the last day ship next month, so they belong to next month.

questions.prompt: November shop forecast: 30 orders a day for 30 days, at a $40 average order. Plus 2 corporate boxes already signed at $5,000 each. What's the forecast?
questions.hint: Orders x average value, then add the contracts.
working: Now you only watch two numbers: orders per day and average order value.
whyNot: $36,000 is the shop on its own. The 2 corporate boxes are signed, so add their $10,000.
$36,000 + $5,000 = $41,000 counts only one box. There are 2 at $5,000 each.

penalty.prompt: The season ticket deadline is in {days} days. {done} are paid, {booked} are reserved, and you're selling {rate} a day. How many will you close at?
penalty.hint: Done, plus booked, plus days left times sales a day.

traps.why: You left out the {booked} reserved seats. They're booked, so count them.
You stopped at today. There are still {days} days of selling at {rate} a day.

call.title: The Christmas shirt order
call.prompt: The kit supplier needs your Christmas order today. Done plus booked plus run rate says you'll sell 900 shirts. Each shirt sold makes $40. Each unsold shirt gets cleared at a $10 loss.

options.label: Order 600 to be safe
options.result: 600 x $40 = $24,000. Then you sell out, and 900 - 600 = 300 fans who wanted a shirt go without.

options.label: Order 900, as forecast
options.result: Good call. 900 x $40 = $36,000. Done plus booked plus run rate is the best guess you have, so use it.

options.label: Order 1,500 so we never run out

takeaway: Done, plus booked, plus run rate times days left. Then times the average value.
